This page corresponds to the precise occupation O*NET/SOC 51-9195.04 Glass Blowers, Molders, Benders, and Finishers: shaping molten glass according to patterns. The official scope text reads: Shape molten glass according to patterns. O*NET's core tasks include: heating glass to a workable state with a gas flame or furnace and rotating it so the heat is even (importance 94); forming, bending or joining glass sections with paddle, flattening and smoothing hand tools or cork (90); blowing tubing into a specified shape with compressed air or the maker's own breath, or blowing and rotating a gather in moulds and on plates to obtain the final shape (87); cutting tubing to specified dimensions with a file or cutting wheel (85); inspecting, weighing and measuring products with instruments such as micrometers, calipers, magnifiers and rulers to verify they meet specifications (85); developing glass product sketches into blueprint specifications (83); recording manufacturing information such as output and dimensions or types (82); determining the type and quantity of glass needed to make a product (82); designing and creating glass objects with blowpipes, hand tools and equipment (79); operating and maintaining finishing machines to grind, drill, sand, bevel, decorate, clean or polish glass or glass products (75); operating an electric kiln to heat and mould glass sheets to the shape and curvature of a metal fixture (70); and placing electrodes at the pipe end and heating and fusing them with a glass torch (64). Supplementary tasks include: tapping the finished piece's neck to separate it from the blowpipe (69); fitting a rubber hose at the pipe end and inflating the pipe (69); placing glass into a press mould and controlling the press to form glassware parts or optical blanks (68); repairing broken spools by replacing the pipe section (65); spraying or wiping an oil solution onto moulds to prevent glass from sticking (61); stacking bent tubing on an asbestos pattern to ensure accuracy (61); setting and adjusting press stroke length and pressure and adjusting furnace temperature according to the type of glass to be worked (60); and applying surface decoration such as coloured glass, enamel and lustre. O*NET marks this occupation as Bright Outlook. The wage, employment and industry figures on this page use the parent occupation 51-9195.00 (Molders, Shapers, and Casters, Except Metal and Plastic) measure presented by O*NET on that page, not the precise occupation 51-9195.04's own measure; the measures and boundaries are set out in the sections below. The asbestos pattern wording in the original source is not a modern materials recommendation, and this page gives no handling operations; actual materials must be checked against safety training and a workplace assessment.

If you are willing to work long term between high heat, open flame and fine handwork, can keep temperature, viscosity and shape within tolerance by feel and eye and are willing to try and inspect repeatedly, and are also happy to work under protection and safety requirements, this occupation's daily demands are closer to your way of working.

Caution signals | O*NET also shows (51-9195.04, percentage response basis): exposure to minor burns, cuts, bites or stings 70% daily; exposure to very hot or very cold temperatures 50% daily; wearing common protective or safety equipment 96% daily; using hands to handle, control or feel objects, tools or controls 83% continually or almost continually; repetitive motions 30% continually or almost continually and 43% more than half the time; importance of being exact or accurate 52% extremely important. This occupation works with molten glass, open flame, kilns, moulds and finishing equipment, and one failure to follow protection requirements near a furnace body or hot glass, one mishandling of kiln temperature or gas or electricity, one wrong annealing or cooling curve, or one misjudged mould, fixture or dimension can cause personal burns, equipment damage and batch scrap, and may also involve gas and electricity safety, dust, noise, high-temperature work and occupational health management systems. O*NET lists this occupation in Job Zone 1-2 (little to some preparation); the entry education requirement is relatively low, but the safety requirements of high-temperature and hazardous work are not low; if you find it hard to face high heat, open flame, dust and noise long term, find it hard to accept burn risk and the ups and downs of feel and eye, or are unwilling to take responsibility for the traceability of dimensional, appearance and process records, these should be treated as real costs that need careful weighing.

Core idea of adjacent roles | most roles in the same and adjacent groups aim to process materials into products that meet requirements within the boundaries of authorization, safety and process and to leave a trace; they differ in object, outputs and authorization level: some take molten glass and hand and kiln processes as their object, some take non-metallic material forming and casting, some take stone, metal or wood machining, and some take welding and brazing or feeding and cutting.

Core purpose of this occupation | with molten glass, open flame, kilns, moulds and finishing equipment as its object, complete hand and equipment work within the boundaries of drawing, process, safety and authorization: heating and gathering, forming, bending and joining, annealing and cooling, cutting, finishing and decoration, inspection and records, so that products meet the drawing, tolerance, appearance and safety requirements, process and inspection records are traceable and boundaries can be explained.

Main objects and basis of this occupation | the objects are glass grade and softening and annealing characteristics; open flame, kilns, electric kilns and fixtures; blowpipes, hand tools, moulds and presses; cutting, grinding, polishing and decorating equipment; measuring instruments and inspection specifications; and gas, electricity, high-temperature and dust protection requirements, based on drawings, process cards, product standards, safety production, occupational health and environmental protection requirements and the institution's process and quality systems.

Responsible party for this occupation | this occupation is responsible for the heating, forming, bending, annealing, finishing, inspection and records that the individual performs, and for the work and verification completed according to the drawing, process card and safety and quality requirements; matters involving process finalization, mould design, pressure-bearing and special equipment inspection, and product safety and acceptance conclusions are decided by the role or body holding the corresponding qualifications according to the system, and this occupation does not replace their decisions.

Conclusion boundaries of adjacent roles | conclusions in the same and adjacent groups are mostly limited to the project, process and duty in question and usually do not constitute a determination of product safety, compliance or legal liability; conclusions that cross disciplines or are used for process, inspection or legal purposes have limits on their applicability.

Conclusion boundaries of this occupation | work conclusions state only verifiable process parameters, dimensions, appearance, annealing and inspection records, and distinguish on-site observed facts from judgments, inferences and items pending verification; no unauthorized judgment or promise may be made on matters beyond the individual's authorization (process finalization, mould design, pressure-bearing and special equipment inspection, product safety and acceptance conclusions); when kiln temperature, gas or electrical anomalies, product cracks, out-of-tolerance dimensions, improper annealing or records inconsistent with the site occur, work must stop and be escalated or handed over, and conclusions must also withstand review by supervisors and by process, quality and regulatory checks.

Pre-employment verification notes | the following six items are for checking one by one before applying and starting work, to avoid inferring actual duties and authorization from the job title or promotional wording; the results should be based on written recruitment information, the labour contract, the job description and the process, safety and quality system documents, and should be confirmed continuously after starting. This page only lists verification directions and does not constitute a formal list of conditions for any institution or project. Special note: this occupation often involves open flame, high temperature, molten glass, gas, electricity, dust and noise work, so be sure to confirm the role's specific requirements for safety training, protective equipment, work permits, certification and data disclosure.

entries.answer: The glass blowers, moulders, benders and finishers on this page are the precise occupation O*NET 51-9195.04 (Glass Blowers, Molders, Benders, and Finishers): shaping molten glass according to patterns. Core tasks include heating glass to a workable state with a gas flame or furnace and rotating it so the heat is even (importance 94), forming, bending or joining glass sections with paddle, flattening and smoothing hand tools or cork (90), blowing tubing into a specified shape with compressed air or the maker's own breath, or blowing and rotating a gather in moulds and on plates (87), cutting tubing to specified dimensions with a file or cutting wheel (85), inspecting, weighing and measuring products with micrometers, calipers, magnifiers and rulers (85), developing glass product sketches into blueprint specifications (83), recording manufacturing information such as output and dimensions or types (82), determining the glass type and quantity needed (82), designing and creating glass objects with blowpipes and hand tools (79), operating and maintaining finishing machines (75), operating an electric kiln to heat and mould glass sheets to the shape and curvature of a metal fixture (70) and placing electrodes at the pipe end and heating and fusing them (64), plus supplementary tasks such as tapping the finished piece's neck to separate it from the blowpipe (69), placing glass into a press mould and controlling the press to form it (68) and setting press stroke and pressure according to the type of glass and adjusting furnace temperature (60). Common job titles include Glassblower, Gaffer, Glass Artist, Neon Glass Bender, Glass Lathe Operator and Glass Worker; on the 51-9195.04 page O*NET shows that the occupation's main industry in the US is manufacturing (the industry data on that page come from the parent occupation 51-9195.00) and marks it Bright Outlook. The above uses the US occupation classification measure, and wages and employment use the parent occupation 51-9195.00 measure as presented via O*NET.

subject.summary: Glass Blowers, Molders, Benders, and Finishers correspond to the precise occupation O*NET/SOC 51-9195.04 Glass Blowers, Molders, Benders, and Finishers: shaping molten glass according to patterns, including heating and gathering, forming, bending and joining, annealing and cooling, cutting, grinding and polishing, decorating and inspection; common job titles include Glassblower, Gaffer, Glass Artist, Neon Glass Bender, Glass Lathe Operator and Glass Worker. The official scope text reads: Shape molten glass according to patterns. Measure note: the US wages, employment and industry data that O*NET presents on the 51-9195.04 page are taken from the parent occupation 51-9195.00 (Molders, Shapers, and Casters, Except Metal and Plastic), and this page faithfully labels them as the parent occupation measure and does not call them this precise occupation's own values.
